summary: Independent review of the 4-row, 2-raw-file SILAC (light/heavy, cross-labelled) hCMEC/D3 OGD secretome SDRF. Online parse_sdrf validation (ms-proteomics + human + cell-lines) exits 0 with only warnings. Every controlled value resolves in OLS, every claim was re-checked against PRIDE, the mzTab/PRIDE XML outputs, the raw BAF headers and Cellosaurus. Channel-to-condition mapping matches the protocol and the search-result titles. Minor findings only.

reviewer_context.context: fresh isolated subagent without producer transcript; producer manifest/report treated as untrusted and checked against primary sources

spec_compliance.evidence: Declared templates derived from the 3 comment[sdrf template] columns: ms-proteomics v1.2.0, human v1.1.0, cell-lines v1.1.0 (the versions sdrf-pipelines' registry resolves; the pinned spec submodule is at ms-proteomics 1.1.0, and v1.2.0 is already used in the repo). sdrf-tools contract: all required columns are present (organism, organism part, biological replicate, age, sex, cell line, cellosaurus accession, technical replicate, data file, acquisition method, instrument, cleavage agent, label, fraction identifier). Column order is correct and sdrf-tools structure exits 0. Reserved words are used only where allowed (age 'not available' is allowed; ancestry 'not available' is allowed). Modification syntax is NT/AC/TA/MT. The (source name, assay name, comment[label]) key and the source/biorep/techrep/fraction coordinate are unique across all 4 rows.

ontology_integrity.evidence: OLS4 obo_id lookups (2026-11-13) matched each label and found none obsolete: NCBITaxon:9606 Homo sapiens, UBERON:0001871 temporal lobe, CL:0000115 endothelial cell, PATO:0000461 normal, EFO:0001272 adult, NCIT:C178973 Roswell Park Memorial Institute 1640 Medium, MS:1003462 maXis impact, PRIDE:0000627 Data-dependent acquisition, MS:1001251 Trypsin, MS:1000133 collision-induced dissociation, MS:1000084 time-of-flight, UNIMOD:4 Carbamidomethyl, UNIMOD:35 Oxidation, UNIMOD:188 Label:13C(6), UNIMOD:267 Label:13C(6)15N(4), PRIDE:0000325/0000326 SILAC heavy/light. The free-text treatment is justified: an OLS search of NCIT/EFO for oxygen(-)glucose deprivation and glucose deprivation returns no matching term. sdrf-tools check reports no UNIMOD swaps and no label mismatches.

source_evidence.evidence: PRIDE record re-read: SILAC with cross-labelling (exp1 light=normoxia/heavy=OGD, exp2 reversed); heavy Lys +6 / Arg +10; Maxis Impact Q-TOF; top-20 DDA; 10 ppm / 0.05 Da; Carbamidomethyl C fixed, Oxidation M variable; passage 20-35; -80 C storage; SILAC RPMI 1640-Flex. mzTab PSM tallies: MOD:00544 is on K only (2541 / 5047), MOD:00587 on R, and MOD:00397 on 100% of C (3001/3001, 3287/3287), which supports Label:13C(6) on K and Carbamidomethyl as fixed. Both BAF headers contain 'maXis impact'. Cellosaurus CVCL_U985: female, adult, temporal lobe microvessel, endothelial cell, cross-references PXD002292. Weksler 2005 abstract: 'normal human brain endothelial cells'. Identity asserted: mzTab IDs PXD002292-53693/53692 and the project title match.

file_mapping.evidence: The live PRIDE files/all listing (every entry has projectAccessions [PXD002292]) holds exactly 2 RAW files, analysis_exp1.baf and analysis_exp2.baf. Both are referenced, each by 2 rows (one per SILAC channel). No peak lists or missing files. The exp1/exp2 file names match the mzTab titles 'experiment 1 Nm L_OGD H' (F070443) and 'experiment 2 Nm H_OGD L' (F070441).

design_consistency.evidence: 2 conditions x 2 cross-labelled experiments = 4 samples. Light/heavy assignment per row matches the protocol and the titles (row1 normoxia light, row2 OGD heavy, row3 OGD light, row4 normoxia heavy). Biological replicate 1/2 = independent experiments, which balances the label swap across conditions. One unfractionated injection per mixture, so technical replicate=1 and fraction=1. factor value[treatment] equals characteristics[treatment]. convert-openms (producer log) yields 2 conditions x 2 files.

omission_safety.evidence: Every non-reserved value traces to PRIDE, mzTab/PRIDE XML, raw header, Cellosaurus or Weksler 2005. Two values are inferences, both disclosed in the manifest and physically constrained for a Bruker Q-TOF: dissociation CID and ms2 analyzer TOF. Age and ancestry are left 'not available' rather than invented. Nothing is added beyond the evidence. The western-blot replication cultures and the ELISA serum cohort have no deposited MS data and are correctly excluded.

deterministic_validation.evidence: flock <lock> parse_sdrf validate-sdrf -s datasets/PXD002292/PXD002292.sdrf.tsv -t ms-proteomics -t human -t cell-lines (online OLS, reviewer run): exit 0, 3 warnings (free-text treatment x2, hCMEC/D3 not in CLO/BTO/EFO). sdrf-tools structure: exit 0. sdrf-tools score: 100/100. sdrf-tools check: exit 1, its only flag being the same hCMEC/D3 cell-line lookup (see minor finding).

findings.message: 'hCMEC/D3' is the Cellosaurus name (CVCL_U985) but is not a CLO/BTO/EFO label (BTO:0003339 is 'HCMEC/D3 cell'); parse_sdrf warns and sdrf-tools check flags it.
findings.evidence: parse_sdrf warning; OLS BTO:0003339 label. The Cellosaurus name convention is used elsewhere in the repo (PXD066627).

findings.message: CID is inferred rather than stated. 'beam-type collision-induced dissociation' (MS:1000422) would describe a Q-TOF collision cell more exactly.
findings.evidence: The Methods text does not name the activation type.

findings.message: Optional characteristics[individual] (recommended) is absent, and nothing records that the samples are conditioned-medium secretome (the PRIDE sample description is 'conditioned medium').
findings.evidence: mzTab sample[1]-description 'conditioned medium'; sdrf-tools contract marks individual as recommended.

findings.message: The study is an in-vitro ischemic-stroke model. Ischemic stroke is cerebrovascular, not neurodegenerative as the original request worded it. It is included under the campaign criteria file (which lists ischemic stroke); the human contributor should confirm the scope.
findings.evidence: The original request names neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson's; campaign/silac_neurological.md criterion 2 includes ischemic stroke.
